gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Let's take a break,' she said. She ___ taking a break.
gaps.explanation: Suggestions are reported as suggest + -ing (or suggest that we take). Never 'suggested to take'.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

gaps.sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.
